About UKABCS

Connecting Research, Education & Industry

A global academic society building practical pathways for scientific research, capacity building, transparent funding, and open collaboration.

Science advances further when researchers can access the resources, networks, and trust needed to do their best work.

UK Organisation for Biotechnology and Computational Science is a UK-registered non-profit academic society. We work at the meeting point of universities, research centres, industry, and the wider scientific community.

Through funding, education, publishing, conferences, and international collaboration, UKABCS helps turn scientific potential into sustained research capability.

Our direction

Vision and mission, held in balance.

Our vision

To be an international home for equitable, data-driven scientific progress—where researchers can access high-quality resources, peer-reviewed support, and an open community.

Our mission

To advance biotechnology and computational science through transparent funding, specialist education, open science, and partnerships that address real global challenges.

How we work

Values that shape every programme.

01

Excellence

We support rigorous, reproducible work and thoughtful peer review.

02

Equity & inclusion

Opportunity should not depend on geography, background, or access to resources.

03

Transparency

Funding decisions, governance, and reporting remain clear and accountable.

04

Collaboration

We connect researchers, institutions, industry, and communities across borders.

05

Innovation

We help practical science move from promising ideas to useful research capability.

06

Sustainability

Our programmes build durable skills, networks, and research capacity.

Strategic priorities

Building the conditions for better science.

Our priorities connect funding, capability, knowledge, and partnerships into a long-term ecosystem.

  1. 01

    Build global research capacity

    Create equitable routes to training, computing resources, mentoring, and international research networks.

  2. 02

    Provide competitive research grants

    Support high-potential projects through transparent, peer-reviewed grant calls.

  3. 03

    Offer continuous education

    Deliver accessible courses, workshops, conferences, and professional development.

  4. 04

    Promote open scientific publishing

    Advance open access, reproducibility, and useful scientific knowledge.

  5. 05

    Strengthen cross-sector partnerships

    Bring universities, research centres, industry, and funders into productive collaboration.
